insights.insight: Verified receipt signals settle at ~$0.10 per confirmed purchase event versus $5–$150 CPA for probabilistic ad tech attribution — a 50–200x cost difference that is structural, not marginal, because the receipt eliminates the attribution problem entirely rather than estimating around it.

insights.topic: Cookie deprecation creates a vacuum this fills
insights.insight: With Chrome joining Safari and Firefox in deprecating cross-site cookies, and device fingerprinting increasingly blocked by privacy regulation, the ad industry has no remaining scalable deterministic signal — verified receipt protocols represent the only cryptographically confirmed purchase event outside a closed first-party ecosystem.

insights.topic: Category breadth confirms everyday commerce coverage
insights.insight: The 14-day receipt mix spans grocery, dining, retail, gas, and pharmacy — topped by Walmart (85 receipts), Costco (29), and Target (28) — meaning this is not a niche or enthusiast data set but a cross-category view of mass-market consumer spending.

insights.topic: Platform silo blind spots remain unresolved
insights.insight: Amazon knows Amazon purchases; Walmart knows Walmart purchases; neither knows the other, and no identity-attached data broker solves this without creating privacy liability — a cross-ecosystem verified signal layer is the only mechanism that makes aggregate spend visible without exposing individual identity.

insights.topic: Social graph diffusion, not geographic cascade
insights.insight: Non-metro activations in AZ, AR, KY, OH, NJ, and MN entered in the same burst cycles despite sharing no borders, confirming the diffusion vector is social graph topology — which means reach projections based on geographic adjacency models will systematically underestimate actual penetration speed.

Traditional attribution depends on lookback windows and modeled conversions that degrade over time and across devices; a cryptographically signed receipt is the conversion event itself, meaning there is no modeling error, no pixel dependency, and no identity attachment required to confirm a purchase occurred.
